commits.message:
perf(ci): compile the corpus dependency tree once, not once per contract

Each of the nine contracts under tests/corpus/contracts is an independent
cargo workspace depending on the same soroban-sdk, and each built into its own
target directory. The SDK dependency tree was therefore compiled nine times per
run, and none of it was cached: Swatinem/rust-cache only covers the root
target/. This dominated the `Run tests` step, the slowest step on both runners
at 605s (ubuntu) and 1351s (windows).

Point every contract build and its dylint pass at one shared target directory,
and add that directory to the cache. Locally the nine per-contract target dirs
totalled 13.4GB and are now untouched; the shared directory is 1.5GB and the
corpus suite completes in 115s from cold.

Also drop the `Build corpus contracts` step, which pre-built three of the nine
into per-contract directories the suite no longer uses, and pin the rust-cache
identity with an explicit shared-key: the default key embeds the job name, so
renaming a job silently discards every cache entry.
